sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: No macro-signals series crosses the extreme threshold (|z| >= 2) heading into the week -- every reading in the strip is elevated at most. The two strongest are 20y+ Treasuries (TLT) at z=-1.93, a three-year price low consistent with a persistent bond bear market, and the Nasdaq 100 at z=+1.89, near the top of its three-year range. Gold (z=+1.60) and WTI crude (z=+1.00) are also elevated but well short of stretched. The S&P 500 closed 2026-08-21 at 7,674.37, up roughly 2.3% over the trailing month and itself elevated at z=+1.88 versus its own three-year mean. Equities pushing higher while long-duration bonds sell off is a real divergence, but nothing in the strip signals a stress event this week.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: 25 operating names in the SP500/R1000/core universe report this week, concentrated Tue-Thu. Tue: MDT reports into a healthcare cohort running flat (-0.12% median 3-day reaction, 431 names) and ULTA into consumer-cyclical, also soft (-0.57% median, 423 names). Wed is heaviest: AVAV reports into industrials, this week's softest cohort at -1.28% median (517 names), AVGO -- the week's largest print -- into technology holding roughly flat (+0.45% median, 475 names), and BF/B into consumer-defensive (-0.51% median, 297 names). Thursday brings LULU back into that same soft consumer-cyclical cohort and CPRT into industrials alongside AVAV's read-through.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table this week at +6.62% median 3-day move across 151 tickers on a thick 2,626-item news window. Copper is next at +2.63% median across just 6 tickers (247 news items -- not thick). Oil-gas sits at the other end, -2.17% median across 33 names on a thick 1,146-item window -- the only top-3 sector moving against the broader commodity complex.
